text.p: The following are leading domestic stories in Portuguese newspapers.
- Police investigate Lisbon-based financial consultant Paramount Consulting for alleged dealing in "phantom" international shares.
- Cabinet approves new draft law on state guarantees. It would widen the potential beneficiaries but tighten controls.

- Prime Minister Antono Guterres' popularity falls to lowest since he elected in October 1995. Support for Socialists drops to 33 percent of the voters against 31 percent for opposition Social Democrats.
- The strategy of the state electricity company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal includes making alliances with Spain and diversifying into telecomunications, real estate, gas and financial area.
- TAP pilots suggest airline use Germany's Lufthansa as model for deal on working practices.
- Quarterly revenues of the factoring sector fell 17.9 percent to 2.6 billion escudos against same period last year.

- Four of the biggest private financial Portuguese groups- Banco Comercial Portugues, Banco Portugues de Investimentos, Banco Espirito Santo and Banco Mello - are developing strategy to take shareholder control of state electricity company EDP-Electricidade de Portugal, after privatisation, and Portugal Telecom.

- The Insurance Nederlands Group (ING) is negociating with Jardim Goncalves, chairman of Banco Comercial Portugues (BCP), to buy the 20 percent stake BCP holdings in the insurance company Mundial Confianca.
